note: DRAFT v1 module checks and final designation exam for the CARSI Trauma & Biohazard Decontamination Practitioner course. Original CARSI questions written for Australian and New Zealand conditions; no IICRC standard text reproduced. SME review and sign-off required before seeding.

quizzes.title: CARSI Trauma & Biohazard Decontamination Practitioner — Module 1 check

questions.questionText: Which workplace safety law applies to a trauma decontamination job in Christchurch?
options: The model WHS Act as implemented in New South Wales
The Victorian Occupational Health and Safety Act 2004
No workplace law applies to cleaning contractors
The Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 (HSWA)
questions.explanation: New Zealand work is governed by HSWA 2015, which puts the primary duty on the PCBU. The model WHS laws apply in Australian jurisdictions except Victoria.

questions.questionText: Which Australian jurisdiction has not implemented the model WHS laws?
options: Queensland
Victoria
Tasmania
The ACT
questions.explanation: Safe Work Australia states the model laws are implemented in all jurisdictions except Victoria, which uses its Occupational Health and Safety Act 2004.

questions.questionText: What makes trauma and biohazard decontamination different from ordinary cleaning?
options: It combines biological, sharps, chemical and psychological hazards that must be controlled before work starts
It uses stronger fragrances to cover odours
It is always done by the property owner
It never needs a written method statement
questions.explanation: The work exposes the crew to blood-borne viruses, sharps, concentrated chemicals and traumatic material, so hazards are assessed and controlled first.

questions.questionText: When may decontamination of a scene begin?
options: As soon as the family asks you to start
Before police arrive, to save time
After police, and the coroner where involved, have released the scene and a person with authority has instructed you
Whenever the neighbours complain about the smell
questions.explanation: Work starts only after release and on the instruction of someone with authority over the property; record who released it and who instructed you.

questions.questionText: A family member wants to walk into the affected room while you work. What do you do?
options: Let them in if they promise not to touch anything
Keep them out of the contaminated zone and explain kindly why
Hand them a pair of gloves and let them help
Leave the door open so they can watch
questions.explanation: Your duty extends to others affected by the work, including family. The contaminated zone is for people in full PPE only.

questions.questionText: You find a box of photographs and jewellery in the affected bedroom. What is the right approach?
options: Ask before moving or discarding personal items, and set keepsakes aside for the family where they can be cleaned or bagged
Discard everything in the room to be safe
Keep valuable items for safekeeping at your depot without telling anyone
Photograph the items and post them to show the job
questions.explanation: Personal items belong to the family. Ask first, set them aside safely, and never share images of a job.

quizzes.title: CARSI Trauma & Biohazard Decontamination Practitioner — Module 2 check

questions.questionText: Which three blood-borne viruses matter most in this work in Australia and New Zealand?
options: Influenza, measles and hepatitis A
Tetanus, hepatitis A and norovirus
Hepatitis B, hepatitis C and HIV
COVID-19, chickenpox and HIV
questions.explanation: healthdirect names hepatitis B, hepatitis C and HIV as the major blood-borne viruses in Australia.

questions.questionText: A worker with a cut on his knuckle touches a dried stain bare-handed. Which exposure route is this?
options: A sharps injury
A mucous membrane splash
No route: dried blood cannot transmit a virus
Contact with non-intact skin
questions.explanation: Broken skin lets fluid in. Cover cuts with a waterproof dressing and glove up before touching any stain, wet or dry.

questions.questionText: Why are standard precautions applied on every trauma job?
options: Because the family always tells you the health status
Only when the deceased was known to be unwell
Because they replace the need for a risk assessment
Because you cannot tell by looking whether blood carries a virus
questions.explanation: Standard precautions treat all blood and body fluids as potentially infectious, whatever the source.

questions.questionText: In Australia, who is the Immunisation Handbook's hepatitis B recommendation for workers aimed at?
options: Only hospital doctors and nurses
People whose work involves handling human tissue, blood or body fluids, or used needles, who are not immune
Only people over 60
Nobody: hepatitis B vaccine is for travel only
questions.explanation: The Handbook recommends hepatitis B vaccine for non-immune people whose work involves handling blood, body fluids or used needles.

questions.questionText: What is the first thing to do after a needlestick injury on site?
options: Wash the wound with soap and water for at least 30 seconds, then go straight to a doctor or emergency department
Squeeze the wound hard to push the blood out
Finish the job, then see a doctor next week
Pour disinfectant into the wound and carry on
questions.explanation: healthdirect advises washing for at least 30 seconds and getting medical advice immediately. Do not squeeze the wound.

questions.questionText: If HIV post-exposure prophylaxis is recommended, when should it start?
options: Within 14 days
Only after the source person is tested
As soon as possible, and within 72 hours
After the 3-dose hepatitis B course is finished
questions.explanation: The ASHM national guidelines say PEP should start as soon as possible and within 72 hours; the earlier the better.

quizzes.title: CARSI Trauma & Biohazard Decontamination Practitioner — Module 3 check

questions.questionText: Which control is the most effective on the hierarchy?
options: Wearing a respirator
Eliminating the hazard
Writing a procedure
Putting up a warning sign
questions.explanation: Elimination is the best way to manage risk; administrative controls and PPE are the least effective.

questions.questionText: Under New Zealand's GRWM Regulations 2016, when is PPE used?
options: To minimise any risk that remains after higher-order and administrative controls
As the first control on every job
Only when the client asks for it
Instead of a risk assessment
questions.explanation: Regulation 6 places PPE last: if a risk remains after other controls, the PCBU ensures suitable PPE is provided and used.

questions.questionText: The crew finds a second affected room halfway through the job. What happens to the SWMS?
options: Carry on with the original SWMS
Throw it away; it no longer applies
Stop, reassess and revise the SWMS, then re-brief the crew
Revise it after the job is finished
questions.explanation: A SWMS is written for the site as found. When the site changes, work stops until the hazards and controls are updated and briefed.

questions.questionText: A surgical mask is offered for scraping dried blood. Why is it not enough?
options: It is too hot to wear
Surgical masks are banned in Australia
It protects better than a respirator, so it is overkill
It protects against large droplet splashes only, not small particles or aerosols
questions.explanation: WorkSafe Queensland notes surgical masks protect against splashes of large droplets only. Scraping and scrubbing can make particles that need a respirator.

questions.questionText: What must happen before a worker first wears a tight-fitting respirator?
options: They read the box
They pass a fit test
They shave once a month
Nothing, provided it is the right size
questions.explanation: SafeWork SA states workers must pass a fit test before first wearing a tight-fitting respirator, then fit-check it each time it goes on.

questions.questionText: When taking PPE off in the transition zone, what comes off first?
options: The outer gloves, the dirtiest item
The respirator
The eye protection
The inner gloves
questions.explanation: Doffing starts with the most contaminated item and ends with hand hygiene, so clean hands are never contaminated by dirty gear.

quizzes.title: CARSI Trauma & Biohazard Decontamination Practitioner — Module 4 check

questions.questionText: In which zone does PPE come off and waste get sealed?
options: The clean zone
The contaminated zone
The client's kitchen
The transition zone
questions.explanation: The transition zone sits between dirty and clean; it is where bags are sealed, tools wiped and PPE removed.

questions.questionText: Why is the visible edge of a carpet stain not taken as the boundary of removal?
options: Carpet always needs to be removed wall to wall
Because the insurer pays by the square metre
Because the stain will spread overnight
Fluids migrate into underlay, the floor beneath and nearby gaps beyond what shows on the surface
questions.explanation: Blood and body fluids travel below and beyond the surface stain, so the crew inspects and cuts past the visible edge.

questions.questionText: Which material is usually removed rather than cleaned in place?
options: Ceramic floor tiles
A glass window
A mattress saturated with blood
A stainless steel bench
questions.explanation: Porous materials saturated with blood cannot be reliably cleaned through; non-porous surfaces are usually cleaned and disinfected.

questions.questionText: Why must a surface be cleaned before a disinfectant is applied?
options: Cleaning makes the disinfectant smell better
It is only needed for carpets
Dirt and grime stop the disinfectant reaching the surface or working properly
The disinfectant is cheaper that way
questions.explanation: Department of Health guidance says thorough cleaning must come before disinfection, because soil blocks contact and affects how well the product works.

questions.questionText: In Australia, a disinfectant label claims it kills viruses. What does that mean for the product?
options: It is a specific claim, so the product must be listed on the ARTG before supply
It needs no regulation
It must be registered with the local council
It may only be used in hospitals
questions.explanation: The TGA treats claims against viruses, spores, tuberculosis, mycobacteria or fungi as specific claims requiring ARTG listing.

questions.questionText: A label directs 20 mL of concentrate per litre. How much goes into a 5 L bucket?
options: 20 mL
100 mL
50 mL
250 mL
questions.explanation: 20 mL per litre multiplied by 5 L is 100 mL. Measure it with a graduated jug, never by eye.

quizzes.title: CARSI Trauma & Biohazard Decontamination Practitioner — Module 5 check

questions.questionText: Where must a used needle never be placed?
options: In a rigid sharps container
Beside the container while you fetch tongs, on a stable tray
In a sharps container held by its handle
In a waste bag
questions.explanation: Sharps must never be placed in waste bags. They go straight into a rigid, puncture-resistant sharps container.

questions.questionText: How should the sharps container move during a search?
options: Carry the container to the sharp
Carry the sharp to the container in your hand
Throw sharps into the container from a distance
Leave sharps for the client to collect
questions.explanation: Bringing the container to the sharp keeps the distance the sharp travels, and the chance of a slip, as short as possible.

questions.questionText: Which standard replaced AS 4031 and AS/NZS 4261 for sharps containers?
options: AS/NZS 1716
questions.explanation: AS/NZS 23907:2023 amalgamated and replaced the older single-use and reusable container standards. Check which edition your regulator names.

questions.questionText: How full may a clinical waste bag be filled?
options: Right to the top, then compacted
No more than two-thirds of its capacity
Three-quarters, then taped
As full as it will hold if double-bagged
questions.explanation: NSW Health policy says waste bags must not be filled beyond two-thirds, so they can be closed securely without compaction.

questions.questionText: In Victoria, a paid job produces 144 L of clinical waste. What does transport require?
options: Nothing, if it is double-bagged
A permitted transporter and a Waste Tracker record
Only a council skip permit
A note to the landlord
questions.explanation: Clinical waste (R100) is reportable priority waste in Victoria. The exemption applies only to loads under 50 litres carried for no fee or reward.

questions.questionText: Which New Zealand standard covers the management of healthcare waste?
options: AS/NZS 3112
AS/NZS 1715
NZS 3604
questions.explanation: NZS 4304:2002 Management of Healthcare Waste sets out classification, packaging, labelling, transport and disposal; councils set local rules.

quizzes.title: CARSI Trauma & Biohazard Decontamination Practitioner — Module 6 check

questions.questionText: Under Australian WHS law, what does "health" include?
options: Both physical and psychological health
Physical health only
Only injuries that need hospital treatment
Only illnesses caused by chemicals
questions.explanation: The model WHS Act defines health as physical and psychological health, so traumatic exposure is a workplace hazard.

questions.questionText: Which Victorian regulations on psychosocial hazards commenced on 1 December 2025?
options: The model WHS Regulations 2011
The Occupational Health and Safety (Psychological Health) Regulations 2025
The Environment Protection Regulations 2021
The GRWM Regulations 2016
questions.explanation: WorkSafe Victoria confirms the Psychological Health Regulations commenced on 1 December 2025 and include traumatic events or content.

questions.questionText: Which is a control Safe Work Australia gives for workers exposed to traumatic events?
options: Ask workers to keep their feelings to themselves
Send the same person to every traumatic job
Increase breaks, recovery time and support
Remove all breaks so the job finishes faster
questions.explanation: Safe Work Australia lists more breaks, recovery time and support, rotating roles, and honest job information among its controls.

questions.questionText: What does the supervisor confirm in the handover walk-through?
options: That the room smells of fragrance
That the family has paid in full
That the photographs look good for marketing
No visible residue, all marked porous material removed, full contact times achieved and no remaining odour source
questions.explanation: Verification is a check of the result in good light, followed by a client walk-through and sign-off recorded in the job file.

questions.questionText: A client says "skip the paperwork, we trust you". Does your safety duty move to the client?
options: Yes, once the client signs a waiver
Yes, if the job is under 10 m²
Only in New Zealand
No. A duty holder cannot transfer their duties to another person
questions.explanation: Safe Work Australia states duties are not transferable, and HSWA 2015 s 31 says the same in New Zealand. Keep the file.

questions.questionText: What is the free call-or-text support number in New Zealand?
questions.explanation: In New Zealand, call or text 1737 any time to talk with a trained counsellor. 13 11 14 is Lifeline in Australia; 0800 764 766 is the NZ Poisons Centre.

quizzes.title: CARSI Trauma & Biohazard Decontamination Practitioner — Final designation exam

questions.questionText: A Melbourne job sits under which workplace safety law?
options: The Victorian Occupational Health and Safety Act 2004
The model WHS Act as adopted in Victoria
The NZ Health and Safety at Work Act 2015
No law, as it is a private home
questions.explanation: Victoria is the one Australian jurisdiction that has not implemented the model WHS laws; WorkSafe Victoria regulates its OHS Act 2004.

questions.questionText: Which statement about blood-borne virus exposure routes is correct?
options: Only sharps injuries can transmit a virus
Intact skin absorbs viruses readily
Dried blood carries no risk at all
Sharps injuries, splashes to mucous membranes and contact with broken skin are the main work routes
questions.explanation: Queensland Health names percutaneous injury and mucous membrane or non-intact skin contact as the occupational exposure routes.

questions.questionText: In New Zealand, how is hepatitis B vaccine listed for adults at occupational risk?
options: Not recommended
Recommended, but not funded
Recommended and funded for all workers
Compulsory by law
questions.explanation: The NZ Immunisation Handbook lists occupational risk under "recommended, not funded"; it is funded after a needle-stick injury.

questions.questionText: There is no post-exposure prophylaxis for which blood-borne virus?
options: HIV
Hepatitis B
Hepatitis C
All three have PEP
questions.explanation: Queensland Health notes no PEP is available for hepatitis C, which is why prevention is critical. PEP exists for HIV and hepatitis B.

questions.questionText: Which respirator standard should workplace respirators comply with?
options: AS/NZS 3816
AS/NZS 1716
AS/NZS 23907
AS/NZS 3112
questions.explanation: WorkSafe Queensland says respirators used at work should comply with AS/NZS 1716. Fit-test before first use.

questions.questionText: What is wrong with spraying disinfectant on a soiled bench and wiping it after ten seconds?
options: Nothing, provided the product smells strong
The bench should have been sanded first
The surface was not cleaned first and the product did not stay wet for its contact time
Disinfectant should always be wiped off immediately
questions.explanation: Clean first, then apply at the label rate and keep the surface wet for the full contact time stated on the label.

questions.questionText: In New Zealand, which agency approves and classifies hazardous substances such as disinfectants?
options: The Environmental Protection Authority (EPA NZ)
The Therapeutic Goods Administration
The local district council
Safe Work Australia
questions.explanation: EPA NZ approves and classifies hazardous substances; WorkSafe NZ enforces workplace requirements. The TGA is Australian.

questions.questionText: Which product claim in Australia triggers ARTG listing before supply?
options: A claim that it smells fresh
A claim that it removes dirt
A claim that the disinfectant kills viruses
A claim that it is made in Australia
questions.explanation: Kill claims against viruses, spores, tuberculosis, mycobacteria or fungi are specific claims that require ARTG listing.

questions.questionText: In New South Wales, how is clinical and related waste classified?
options: As general solid waste
As special waste
As recyclable waste
As household waste if double-bagged
questions.explanation: NSW EPA has pre-classified clinical and related waste as special waste, with specific transport and management requirements.

questions.questionText: Used sharps are found on a commercial site. Where can they go?
options: Only into an approved rigid sharps container for the clinical waste stream
General rubbish if wrapped in tape
The recycling bin
A waste bag inside a box
questions.explanation: WorkSafe ACT states used sharps cannot be placed in general rubbish or recycling at a workplace; NSW Health says never in waste bags.

questions.questionText: A 72 L clinical waste bag may hold at most how much?
questions.explanation: Two-thirds of 72 L is 48 L. Filling no further lets the bag close securely without compaction.

questions.questionText: Which hazard does Safe Work Australia name that is central to trauma work?
options: Exposure to loud music
Long commutes to the depot
Working with computers
Exposure to traumatic events or materials
questions.explanation: Safe Work Australia names exposure to traumatic events or materials as a psychosocial hazard that PCBUs must manage.

questions.questionText: In New Zealand, how does HSWA define health?
options: Physical health only
Physical and mental health
Freedom from infectious disease only
Whatever the employer decides
questions.explanation: WorkSafe NZ confirms HSWA defines health as physical and mental health, so psychosocial risks must be managed.

questions.questionText: A worker lifts a mattress at 9:00 am Monday and feels a needlestick. By when must HIV PEP start if recommended?
options: By 9:00 am the following Monday
Within 24 hours or never
As soon as possible, and no later than 9:00 am Thursday
Only after a hepatitis B blood test
questions.explanation: The window is 72 hours: 9:00 am Monday plus 72 hours is 9:00 am Thursday. Earlier is better, so the worker is assessed the same day.

questions.questionText: Which record belongs in a defensible job file?
options: Each disinfectant used, with its ARTG number or NZ label, the dilution, the area and the contact time
Social media posts about the job
Photographs of the family
A summary written a month later from memory
questions.explanation: Records made as the work happens show what was done. Product, dilution, area and contact time prove the disinfection step.
